deep.reconstruction:
This page has no derivation. It is a table, and it continues the previous page (columns 661–827, same rows) and the next page (rows 953–997 against columns 2–89). Together these pages form a large chart of quadratic-residue characters between pairs of primes below 1000.

Layout of this sheet:
- Rows are the primes p = 439, 443, 449, 457, 461, 463, 467, 479, 487, 491, 499, 503, 509, 521, and 523 (523 in red).
- Columns are the 24 primes q = 829, 839, ..., 997.
- A small circle in cell (p, q) means that the column prime q is a quadratic residue modulo the row prime p, i.e. legendre(q, p) = +1 (my identification). A blank means q is a non-residue mod p.
- Horizontal and vertical strokes join circles in adjacent cells. They carry no arithmetic content; they appear to be a visual aid for checking or comparing patterns.
- Rows 509 and 521 are still empty. Row 523 was added in red ink without connecting strokes, so the table was being filled row by row and was unfinished.

How I identified the meaning, by hand computation with quadratic reciprocity (my checks, not on the page):
- Row 523 is circled under exactly 857, 883, 887, 907, 919, 953, 967, 971, 977 and 991. Spot checks:
  - (857/523) = (334/523) = (2/523)(167/523) = (-1)(-1) = +1.
  - (883/523) = (360/523) = (2/523)(5/523) = (-1)(-1) = +1.
  - (953/523) = (2·5·43/523) = +1.
  - (829/523) = -(17/523) = -1.
  - (839/523) = (79/523) = -1.
  - (853/523) = (2·3·5·11/523) = -1.
  - (911/523) = (97/523) = -1.
  - (941/523) = -1.
  - (997/523) = -1.
  All of these agree with the circles and blanks.
- Row 439 has circles at 839, 857, 863, 883, 887, 907, 929, 941, 947, 971, 977 and 991. Checks:
  - (839/439) = (400/439) = +1.
  - (857/439) = (2·11·19/439) = +1.
  - (929/439) = (3·17/439) = +1.
  - (829/439) = (2·3·5·13/439) = -1, and 829 is blank.
- The direction of the symbol matters when both primes are ≡ 3 (mod 4). For p = 439 and q = 883: (883/439) = (5/439) = +1 but (439/883) = -1, and the cell is circled. Likewise (883/523) = +1 but (523/883) = -1, and that cell is circled. So the circle encodes 'column prime is a residue of the row prime'.

Purpose: an extensive empirical table of the Legendre character (q/p) for primes up to 1000. It extends the small residue table (Tabula II) of the Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801). It could serve empirical study of reciprocity, of distribution patterns, or as an aid for factoring and for forms computations. No arithmetic is written on the page itself.
errors: Spot checks (row 523 entirely; rows 439, 443 and 467 partially) found no erroneous entries.
Rows 509 and 521 are not filled in. This is incompleteness, not an error.

results.what: Table of quadratic residue characters (q/p) for row primes 439–523 against column primes 829–997. A circle means q is a quadratic residue mod p.
results.modern_name: Table of Legendre symbols / quadratic residue table
results.usually_credited_to: Residue tables: Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), Tabula II for small primes; later larger tables by Jacobi (Canon Arithmeticus, 1839) and others.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a computational table of Legendre symbols, a routine activity Gauss is well known to have done on a large scale. Its size (primes up to 1000) is a minor archival detail. There is no new theorem.

checkable.asserts: The red row 523 is circled exactly at the column primes that are quadratic residues mod 523.
Row 439 is circled exactly at the column primes that are QR mod 439 (according to my reading of the image).
This distinguishes the convention: the circle means column prime q is a QR mod row prime p, not the reverse.
The circle at row 443, column 829 is correct.
The circle at row 467, column 857 is correct.

transcription_corrections: The circles in the body of the table are not arbitrary marks: each marks a cell where legendre(q, p) = +1. The strokes merely join grid-adjacent circles.
The row-523 red circles (857, 883, 887, 907, 919, 953, 967, 971, 977, 991) match the image. 997 is not circled.
There is a faint, partly crossed-out heading at the top ('Math. 1' or similar) and a crossed-out number at the top right. '(11)' is the folio number and '21' (red crayon) is a later foliation.
